governanceNotes: Authored conservatively as ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a systematic review and meta-analysis reports geographic tongue occurring more frequently among psoriasis patients, but a prevalence association establishes neither causation nor aggravation in an individual, and the relationship is most consistent with a shared inflammatory mucocutaneous diathesis.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reports that geographic tongue (benign migratory glossitis) occurs at substantially higher prevalence among patients with psoriasis than in controls, and smaller clinical studies report the co-occurrence of the two mucocutaneous findings.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the reported relationship is a cross-sectional prevalence association, geographic tongue is a benign inflammatory lesion of the tongue dorsum, and no literature demonstrates that geographic tongue caused, worsened, or prolonged psoriasis or vice versa in any individual; the co-occurrence is most consistently framed as a shared inflammatory diathesis rather than a directional pathway.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized shared-immune-pathology pathway has been described: histologic features of geographic tongue (keratinocyte acanthosis, neutrophilic infiltration resembling Munro microabscesses) overlap with psoriatic histopathology, suggesting a common inflammatory mucocutaneous susceptibility, but shared histology would explain co-occurrence without establishing that either condition produces the other, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The meta-analytic evidence reports higher geographic-tongue prevalence in psoriasis populations, and shared histopathologic features are described, but neither condition is demonstrated to cause or aggravate the other in an individual. Dermatology and oral-medicine documentation of both findings, chronology, exclusion of mimics, and competing explanations all require case-specific review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Oral-medicine documentation of geographic tongue against clinical criteria with chronology; dermatology documentation of psoriasis diagnosis, phenotype, and course; exclusion of oral-mimic conditions (fissured tongue, candidiasis, reactive lesions); records addressing whether the two conditions tracked together clinically; competing-explanation review
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Oral candidiasis, fissured tongue, or other mimic lesions of the tongue dorsum
Reactive or drug-related tongue lesions unrelated to psoriasis
Psoriasiform mucosal changes from medication rather than shared diathesis
Nutritional or hematologic contributors to glossitis

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the meta-analytic prevalence association between geographic tongue and psoriasis is well supported, but the relationship is most consistently a shared inflammatory diathesis with no demonstrated directional pathway, so this edge flags the association for evidence-gap review only and must never be presented as established causation or aggravation.
evidenceGaps: Clinical documentation of both conditions with chronology
Specialist assessment excluding oral mimics of geographic tongue
Records addressing temporal co-fluctuation of the two conditions, where available
A medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case

sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis reporting higher geographic-tongue prevalence among psoriasis patients; supports the bounded prevalence-association proposition only, not individual causation or aggravation.
